title: Keeping a working band together
summary: Keeping a consistent group needs lead time and steady work; from Blakey he learned that one man doesn't stop the show.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Is it a challenge to keep a working trio behind you, a consistent group of musicians?

It can be, to a point, but what I feel, if you share with these musicians what you’re trying to do and also if you give enough lead time, if you’re booking in March and now we’re in September, there’s enough lead time to get to a point, the musicians that you want, and sometimes you can’t. But again, that’s what I learned from Art Blakey. No one monkey stops the show. So you should be able to — see now all these things about Art are coming back to me now. You should be able to get someone else and plug them in and you should still be able to present what it is that you would like to present. You should feel like, oh man I don’t have my man on drums, I’m not going to be able to play what I want to play. You see what I mean? You should still be able to present what you want to present. Obviously if you can get a strong nucleus of guys and you can work, but the point of it too is do you have enough work to be able to keep these guys committed to you? I mean you almost have to be on the road all the time which is very difficult. And I know some musicians who stay on the road all the time. And when you’re on the road all the time you can get that commitment because there’s a volume and you’re able to pay musicians a consistent salary. But if you don’t have the consistent salary and all of a sudden something pops up well they’re already committed to something else, they’ve got to work, and I don’t know that I’ve been that kind of artist that’s getting to the point now, I’m usually doing things a couple, two times a month at least, but what about the other two weeks, when they’ve got to feed themselves and the other business things that go along with that. So you have to respect anybody that’s getting work and hopefully you © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
can begin to start booking yourself far enough in advance where you can get the musicians, the ones you want to be available for you.
